purpose: Machine-checkable claim ledger for the consolidated FAFB v783 evidence case.

status_vocabulary.PROVEN: Direct evidence supports the stated claim within its defined scope.
status_vocabulary.REPRODUCED: A deterministic reconstruction reproduced the reference result.
status_vocabulary.INDEPENDENTLY_CORROBORATED: An independent source or route agrees with the result.
status_vocabulary.PARTIAL: Only part of the intended claim is established.
status_vocabulary.NEGATIVE_RESULT: A tested route or hypothesis failed under the stated conditions.
status_vocabulary.BLOCKED: A required external dependency prevented completion.
status_vocabulary.UNRESOLVED: The available evidence is insufficient to decide the claim.
status_vocabulary.INFERENCE_ONLY: The statement is an interpretation rather than a directly established observation.

claims.statement: The four anchor neurons are exactly the specified FAFB v783 root IDs.
All 649 reference synapse-coordinate rows are exact tuple matches in the official Codex FAFB v783 individual-synapse coordinate product.
All 75 selected directed neuron pairs have exact aggregate synapse counts in the official Codex FAFB v783 connections product.
All 649 reference coordinates are independently corroborated by the frozen Zenodo FAFB v783 midpoint mapping.
Each of the four anchor roots occurs exactly once in the published dendrite-analysis table and is marked Dendrite_used=True.
The published NeuRosetta subtree-selection algorithm was deterministically reproduced on the four retained project SWCs.
The historical Point_data.pkl artifact is identified by the recorded source commit, Git blob, and SHA-256 digest.

The exact December 2025 implementation revision that generated Point_data.pkl has not been recovered from the public historical record, although the later public generator algorithm has now been reconstructed.
caveats: The public paper repository was initialized at 2025-12-09T19:26:04Z. Its ANOVA notebook was added at 19:40:07Z and directly reads the local T45_Morpho_data/Data/Pickled_data/Point_data.pkl path. Point_data.pkl was then added at 19:41:50Z as a 3,049,948-byte binary blob. The subsequent 19:42:19Z Point_data commit points to the same blob/tree, so no second binary content revision is exposed. Therefore the December public repository history contains consumption evidence but no committed producer preceding the artifact. Public PP1-PP5/Metrics notebooks were added later in 2026-08, while public NeuRosetta Forest/IO used by that pipeline appears in 2026-01. The later Metrics1 notebook explicitly derives root_x/root_y/root_z from tree.get_root_coordinate() on Reduced_dendrites, and PP3 explicitly creates Reduced_dendrites by subtree extraction plus reduction. This establishes the later public algorithmic lineage but does not cryptographically prove that the December 2025 artifact was generated by that exact revision. A private/local or legacy route remains possible.

The only public conda-environment.yml is a release-era file added on 2026-01-16; it names T45_paper and does not declare NeuRosetta, so it cannot pin the December neurosetta kernel to a specific historical installation.

claims.statement: The mapping from an individual synapse coordinate to a biological synaptic cleft compartment is established by geometry alone.
caveats: Geometry is diagnostic evidence only; direct biological compartment assignment requires independent evidence.

claims.statement: The committed project SWCs are byte-for-byte identical to the unpublished internal morphology artifacts used by the historical study.
caveats: The public historical record does not expose the internal morphology artifact required for a bitwise comparison.

claims.statement: The published T4/T5 morphology method has two manual review boundaries around automated dendrite extraction: soma-root verification/correction before subtree selection, and a second dendrite verification that can modify the selected compartment and correct individual routing/skeletonization errors.
caveats: The publication documents these review stages and their purpose, but no historical per-neuron edit record for the four project anchors has been recovered.
This does not prove which December 2025 software revision or GUI produced the historical edits.

claims.statement: Public NeuRosetta-family code existed before the December 2025 Point_data artifact and included neuron simplification, subtree/root selection, and explicit coordinate transformation/scaling functionality.
caveats: This establishes pre-artifact software-family context only; it does not identify the exact December 2025 producer revision or execution environment.

claims.statement: The public PySide6 NeuRosetta GUI implementation and explicit manual-subtree GUI operation entered that repository's public history in April 2026, after the December 2025 Point_data artifact.
caveats: The April 2026 commit explicitly refers to updating an older GUI, so an unpublished/private predecessor cannot be excluded.

claims.statement: The 649-row canonical V230 synapse-coordinate artifact is linked to the historical Point_data case only through the four shared anchor root IDs; it also contains partner roots and has no row-level morphology join key.
caveats: Shared root IDs do not establish common morphology materialization, common software revision, or common execution run.

claims.statement: The archived January 2026 Submission_release preserves Point_data and downstream analysis artifacts but does not preserve the PP1–PP5 preprocessing notebooks or the Reduced_dendrites intermediate morphology tree.
caveats: This is a release-content boundary, not proof that the omitted producer never existed.

claims.statement: The public PP1→PP2→reduction coordinate path does not contain an implicit affine coordinate transform sufficient to explain the historical Point_data root frame; the public Metrics1 path instead reads root coordinates from Reduced_dendrites after explicit nm-to-um conversion.
caveats: This constrains the public reconstruction; it does not identify the missing December 2025 transform or prove that the later public preprocessing implementation is byte-identical to the historical producer.

claims.statement: A bounded neural observation can deterministically produce a capability candidate and pass that candidate into the existing Leader TaskStep contract; neural activity does not grant permission, network access, or system mutation.
caveats: The current regression uses explicitly opaque/synthetic neural channels and therefore is not evidence that a biological FlyWire neuron currently controls Code Hand.
Biological mapping from FlyWire circuit activity to an action capability remains unestablished.

claims.statement: The four project anchor roots are identified as T4a, T4c, T5a, and T5c, and the published Drosophila T4/T5 motion-system literature supports their subtype-level ON/OFF and canonical motion-direction properties: T4/T5 a=front-to-back, c=upward.
caveats: The functional properties are supported at the cell-type/subtype level; this does not mean that the four exact project root IDs were individually recorded in those functional experiments.
This mapping does not establish that these cells currently receive camera input in this project.
This mapping does not assign a Code Hand capability or prove biological control of the software agent stack.

claims.statement: A live GitHub Actions execution of the pinned TuragaLab/flyvis v1.2.0 model produced continuous MovingEdge response traces for T4a, T4c, T5a, and T5c, and all four observed preferred directions were within the declared 45 degree validation bound.
caveats: This is a model-level runtime result, not an electrical recording of the four exact FAFB v783 root IDs.
Continuous model responses are not converted into spikes in this evidence path.
The result does not establish a camera-driven biological activity source, Code Hand capability mapping, or biological control.

claims.statement: The historical December 2025 Point_data.pkl and the August 2026 Zenodo point_data.pkl are distinct materializations: they preserve the same four anchor IDs and subtype labels but have different binary hashes, row counts/schema, root coordinates, and morphology metrics.
caveats: The comparison proves artifact-level divergence, not which morphology producer or alignment step caused the divergence.
The four anchor rows in the updated evidence are selected by exact Root ID with one unique row per anchor in each snapshot.

The historical file stores Total_Cable in a numerically nanometre-scale representation (~315401 nm for T4a), while the later Metrics1-generated Zenodo values are in micrometre-scale numbers (~318.836); unit interpretation is therefore snapshot-specific.

claims.statement: The four project Point_data anchors are selected by exact FAFB v783 Root ID, with exactly one row per anchor in both the historical December 2025 and later Zenodo snapshots; the historical pickle also contains decoded JAX ArrayImpl object cells.
caveats: The decoded JAX object type identifies a serialization/runtime dependency but does not identify the producer code path that constructed the arrays.
This does not recover the missing December 2025 population-aligned Reduced_dendrites state.

claims.statement: A public GeoJax/legacy-Neurosetta software family contained JAX-backed geometry and PCA operations in snapshots predating the historical Point_data artifact; this is technically compatible context for the historical pickle's JAX ArrayImpl values.
caveats: No exact historical Point_data execution is cryptographically bound to these software snapshots.
Compatibility does not establish producer identity or causation.

claims.statement: A later public PP3 implementation was executed successfully in GitHub Actions on all four project V229 SWCs: it reproduced the expected subtree-selection node IDs, while the resulting root coordinates did not exactly match the historical Point_data roots; a rigid transform also failed to reconcile all four pairs.

The exact historical producer of Point_data.pkl remains unresolved: the public Metrics1 notebook exposes a 23-column metric computation with no persistence call, while the historical artifact has 24 columns including Subtype_evDir_x/y/z that are not exposed by the public notebook or indexed public source.
caveats: The mismatch establishes that the current public Metrics1 notebook is not a complete textual producer for the historical artifact.
It does not by itself identify whether the missing three direction columns were computed by a private/local script, an earlier notebook revision, an uncommitted cell, or a separate augmentation step.

claims.statement: The four project Point_data anchor rows contain Subtype_evDir_x/y/z values that form unit-length direction vectors to numerical precision.
caveats: This proves the stored vector values and their norm, not the algorithm that generated them.
The exact historical computation of Subtype_evDir remains unresolved.

claims.statement: The three historical Subtype_evDir_x/y/z columns are legacy/transitional fields at the public-snapshot level: they exist in the December 2025 Point_data artifact but are absent from the December public README schema and absent from the later August 2026 Zenodo Point_data schema.
caveats: Legacy/internal is an interpretation of the lifecycle evidence, not proof of the private producer implementation.
The exact writer and mathematical definition remain unresolved.

claims.statement: A local Windows execution observed a physical Uniarch Uho-S2E network-camera stream pass through ONVIF discovery, RTSP capture, the 721-receptor BoxEye bridge, and the pinned FlyVis network, producing a finite 20-frame continuous model response.
caveats: The observation was performed on a user's local Windows machine and is not an independently reproduced physical-camera run in GitHub Actions.
Private LAN endpoint, credentials, and device serial information are intentionally omitted from the public evidence artifact.
The claim is limited to the observed software path and does not establish exact FAFB v783 root-level electrical activity, biological spikes, or biological control.

claims.statement: Byte-level inspection of the historical December 2025 Point_data.pkl explicitly finds the private JAX serializer callable `jax._src.array._reconstruct_array`; all eight PCA/angle/direction-vector metric columns are scalar float32 jaxlib._jax.ArrayImpl values across all 5,828 rows.
caveats: The serializer reference identifies the serialization mechanism, not the exact producer code path.
The exact December 2025 JAX version and execution environment remain unresolved.

claims.statement: The historical Point_data.pkl serialization contract matches public JAX source snapshots immediately before and on the artifact date: both expose jax._src.array._reconstruct_array(fun, args, arr_state, aval_state) and ArrayImpl.__reduce__ with aval_state containing weak_type.
caveats: The match establishes serializer-format compatibility, not the exact JAX release or execution environment.
It does not recover the morphology producer script.

claims.statement: Under the standard released JAX ArrayImpl serializer, the historical Point_data pickle's weak_type-only aval_state is compatible with JAX v0.4.31 through v0.8.0, while v0.4.30 is incompatible because its reducer includes named_shape.
caveats: This is not exact JAX version identification.
Private/forked JAX builds and nonstandard serialization paths are outside this release-tag comparison.

claims.statement: If the December 2025 Point_data producer used the same Python 3.10 runtime represented by the contemporaneous neurosetta consumer notebook, then JAX 0.7.x and later are excluded by JAX's Python-version requirement, leaving JAX 0.6.2 or earlier within the released reducer family observed here.
caveats: The consumer notebook does not cryptographically prove it is the producer environment.
A private/forked JAX build or a separate producer environment could violate this conditional bound.

claims.statement: A bounded GitHub public-code search on 2026-10-06 for the historical `Subtype_evDir` schema and combinations with `PC1_angle`/`Point_data` returned no external public repository implementation; all returned hits were within the project's own evidence/tests.
caveats: This is a bounded negative search result, not proof of nonexistence.
Private, deleted, unindexed, or differently named implementations may still exist.

claims.statement: The historical Point_data.pkl contains one distinct normalized 3D Subtype_evDir vector per row across all 5,828 neurons: each of the eight subtype groups has unique triplets under exact float comparison and unit-norm error below 4.7e-7.
caveats: This establishes the numerical structure of the stored vectors, not their semantic origin.
The exact producer operation that generated Subtype_evDir_x/y/z remains unresolved.

claims.statement: The later public Metrics1_Point_data notebook exposes exact unit-conversion, PCA, basis/angle, mesh, and worker-count parameters, but its inspected code snapshot does not compute the historical Subtype_evDir_x/y/z fields and contains no active Point_data pickle persistence call.
caveats: This is a later public code snapshot, not recovered December 2025 producer code.
The notebook markdown says the dataframe is to be saved as pickle, but the inspected code snapshot has no active save/to_pickle operation.
A private or earlier revision may still differ.

claims.statement: A public Neurosetta_legacy_v0.0.1 implementation predating the historical Point_data artifact exposes coord_eig_decomp with robust MinCovDet covariance, eigenvalue normalization, descending sorting, and transposed eigenvectors; this establishes a pre-artifact PCA/eigenvector computational family but does not prove it was the December 2025 producer because the historical pickle serialized all eight metric columns as JAX ArrayImpl values while this function returns NumPy arrays.
caveats: The exact December 2025 producer remains unresolved.
The legacy function's exact dependency versions at artifact-production time are not established.
The historical JAX scalar serialization could result from downstream wrapping or a different producer path.

claims.statement: The first public commit containing the historical Point_data.pkl also contains only a consumer/analysis notebook, ANOVA_analysis.ipynb, which reads Point_data.pkl with pandas.read_pickle and performs downstream ANOVA/ANCOVA analysis; the same commit tree contains no public producer code path.
caveats: This proves only the contents of the public commit tree inspected at the ingest boundary.
It does not exclude private producer code or uncommitted local notebooks outside the public repository.

claims.statement: The public GeoJax history shows that its JAX-based robust covariance/eigendecomposition and signed-angle geometry family entered at commit 4dfc82bbc6dbe37b64a540758d6ea3ed6c9829aa on 2025-02-12 and remained observable through the last public pre-artifact head 33b0f8727ab447eff86e35a69c60c1f33b4d1513 on 2025-05-02; this lineage is strongly compatible with the JAX ArrayImpl type and PCA family observed in historical Point_data, but does not establish the exact December 2025 producer.
caveats: The exact GeoJax revision used by the December 2025 producer is not recovered.
The historical Subtype_evDir_x/y/z computation remains unresolved.
Type/algorithm compatibility is not producer identity.

claims.statement: A public Figure_5 notebook added on 2025-12-10 directly loaded Data/Point_data.pkl in a neurosetta/Python 3.10.17 context, consumed its PC1/PC2/PC3 columns, and passed their type-level means to generate_random_bifurication; the same-date Random_bifurcations source imported GeoJax and used gj.cross/gj.angle/gj.normalize. This proves a contemporaneous Point_data-to-GeoJax consumer bridge, not that GeoJax or that module generated the historical PCA values.
caveats: The bridge begins at Point_data outputs PC1/PC2/PC3 and does not expose their producer.
The exact GeoJax revision installed in the December 2025 environment remains unresolved.
Random_bifurcations consumes PCA values; it is not evidence that it generated them.

claims.statement: The Figure_5 notebook committed on 2025-12-10 resolves Data/Point_data.pkl to exactly the same Git blob b85caf49f45677f2075f7b5f2c8830141cd96d02 that first entered the public repository at the 2025-12-09 Point_data ingest boundary.
caveats: This proves exact artifact consumption by the contemporaneous public notebook.
It does not recover the producer of the artifact or prove the algorithm that created PC1/PC2/PC3.

claims.statement: The historical Subtype_evDir vectors show a subtype-dependent planar angle pattern: the +y convention nearly reproduces PC1_angle for c/d, while the +x convention fits a/b better. This is compatible with, but does not prove, selecting a PC2-like axis for a/b and a PC1-like axis for c/d.
caveats: The recovered historical artifact does not include per-row PCA eigenvector arrays or the December 2025 producer.
T5a and T5b retain substantial angular error under the candidate x-axis convention and have larger median absolute z components.
The exact eigenvector index, transform, and sign/orientation rule remain unresolved.

claims.statement: At the last public GeoJax snapshot before the historical Point_data.pkl ingest (2025-05-02), coord_eig_decomp provided robust JAX PCA with sorted eigenvectors and align_point_cloud accepted a caller-supplied eigenvector order and target basis, applying sign alignment per vector. This proves that configurable eigenvector-order/orientation machinery existed before the artifact, not that this code generated Subtype_evDir.
caveats: align_point_cloud returns aligned coordinates; the source snapshot does not directly define or emit Subtype_evDir_x/y/z.
No producer invocation, subtype-specific order argument, target basis, or December 2025 dependency revision has been recovered.
C-POINTDATA-002 remains UNRESOLVED.

claims.statement: The public paper-repository history proves a consumer-before-artifact sequence: an ANOVA notebook added at 2025-12-09T19:40:07Z reads Point_data.pkl from a machine-local path, 103 seconds before the binary first appears as the sole changed path in commit cd17d34. The later public PP1-PP5/Metrics1_Point_data notebook set was added on 2026-08-10 in the commit that removed tracked Data artifacts. This establishes a public producer-code gap at the historical artifact boundary, not the nonexistence of a private or uncommitted local producer.
caveats: C-POINTDATA-002 remains UNRESOLVED because GitHub's public history cannot establish which local/private script generated the binary.
The later public Metrics1 notebook is not proof of the December 2025 producing implementation.

claims.statement: The present public NeuRosetta repository's initial commit (timestamped 2025-10-21) contains only .gitignore, LICENSE.md, and a 13-byte README. The first PCA utility in its path history appears on 2026-07-27 as a 13-line NumPy SVD module, followed on 2026-07-28 by a 291-line NumPy eig_decomp refactor using numpy.linalg.eigh. This proves the public current NeuRosetta PCA implementation is post-artifact evidence, not proof of the December 2025 producer; local/private or older legacy implementation remains possible.
caveats: The Git author/committer date of the initial repository commit is not a repository-publication timestamp; the repository itself was created 2026-01-20.
No claim is made that equivalent local/private or pre-existing legacy code did not exist.
C-POINTDATA-002 remains UNRESOLVED.
